reaudit_note: Mechanical re-stamp by `./le rfc reseal`. Every verdict re-stamped below was in the SHIFTED state: its recorded unit fingerprints -- the enclosing top-level function of each tagged test -- were byte-identical to the tree, and only the file around them had moved (a line shift, a sibling test, an import rewrite). Nothing about what any of these tests asserts changed, so no verdict was re-judged and only the `tests` map was rewritten. A verdict whose unit, cited producer code, or requirement text moved was REFUSED and left stale for a human. The proof is the code in verdict_freshness(), not this note.

RFC2869-2.1-1.note: Forbidden: a second interim generation for the session entering the retransmission queue while one is outstanding. TestRFC2869InterimLoopKeepsOneGenerationOutstanding ticks at 10ms against a stalled server with a 300ms retransmission budget and fatals if more than 12 datagrams arrive in 1s (per-tick dispatch gives about 100, two outstanding generations about 20); TestRFC2869InterimLoopSendsOnItsInterval fatals below 2 sends, so the bound is not vacuous.

RFC2869-2.1-2.note: Forbidden: the Access-Accept Acct-Interim-Interval winning over a locally configured value. TestRFC2869LocalAcctIntervalOverridesAccessAccept configures 40ms against an Access-Accept of 3600s and fatals if fewer than 3 interim records arrive in 2s; TestRFC2869AbsentAcctIntervalLeavesTheAccessAcceptInCharge fatals if any interim arrives with no local value, so a NAS that ignores the Access-Accept outright fails.

RFC2869-5.14-1.note: All three reply codes now driven through Client.Exchange: Access-Accept (existing pair) and, new, Access-Reject and Access-Challenge whose Response Authenticator verifies (asserted) and whose Message-Authenticator is HMAC-MD5 under another secret are discarded (Exchange errors, no packet); correctly signed Reject and Challenge are delivered with their Reply-Message.

RFC2869-5.19-1.note: Rejudged 2026-10-14 by a reader who did not author the tests. - TestRFC2869EAPBesideAnotherCredentialIsRefused drives EAP-Message beside User-Password, CHAP-Password and now ARAP-Password through Client.Exchange: each errors and no datagram reaches the server. + TestRFC2869EAPOnlyAccessRequestIsSent sends one datagram carrying EAP-Message and none of the other three. The L2TP builder pair covers PAP and CHAP-MD5 carrying only their own credential. User-Password beside CHAP-Password is not driven by this row's units; the same guard (client.go oneCredentialType) refuses it under RFC3579-3.3-2's units.

RFC2869-5.2-1.note: Independent judgment 2026-10-11 (judge did not author a0a101e5ad). RFC 2869 Section 5.2: "This attribute indicates how many times the Acct-Output-Octets counter has wrapped around 2^32 in the course of delivering this service, and can only be present in Accounting-Request records where the Acct-Status-Type is set to Stop or Interim-Update." Positive TestRFC2869OutputGigawordsOnInterimUpdate stubs TxBytes at 3*2^32+200 and requires exact Acct-Output-Octets 200 and Acct-Output-Gigawords 3 on an Interim-Update built by buildAcctPacket: a wrong split (splitGigawords) or a missing attribute fails it. Negative TestRFC2869OutputGigawordsAbsentOnStart builds a Start over the same wrapped counter and requires no attribute 53. Isolation holds: counterDelta is stateless over the session baseline (zero here), so if the Stop/Interim-Update guard in buildAcctPacket admitted Start, the delta would carry 3 gigawords and the attribute would appear; the negative is not passing because counters are unavailable. buildAcctPacket's only callers are the Start, Stop and Interim-Update senders, so Start is the only disallowed status the producer can reach. Stop, also permitted, is untested here but is not an obligation. Both clauses (wrap-count value, presence restricted to Stop/Interim-Update) are asserted exactly. Verdict enforced.

RFC2869-x-2.note: Re-judged 2026-09-30: only the tag comment on TestBuildAcctPacketGigawords changed (it absorbed the wrap-count wording of the retired RFC2869-x-5); the body is unchanged. Clause 1 forbidden: a Gigawords value other than the wrap count; TestBuildAcctPacketGigawords asserts Acct-Input-Gigawords 2 and Acct-Output-Gigawords 3 for 0x200000064 and 0x3000000C8 octets on a Stop, positive re-recorded against acct.go::splitGigawords and observed red. Clause 2 forbidden: Gigawords in a record other than Stop or Interim-Update; TestRFC2869GigawordsAbsentOnStart fails if an Accounting-Start built from >4GB counters carries either attribute. The NAS emits only Start, Interim-Update and Stop (authradius), so Start is the only other status it can send.
